DEVICESETUP.SETUP_NEW_DEVICE: Title or entry button of the new-device setup flow, where the user sets up a freshly powered Volumio player and puts it on their network. 'Configure' = set up. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.INSTRUCTION_STEP_1: Numbered instruction (step 1 of 4) at the start of the new-device setup flow: switch on the music player. Imperative, addressed to the user. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.INSTRUCTION_STEP_2: Numbered instruction (step 2 of 4) in the new-device setup flow: plugging in a network (Ethernet) cable is optional. Imperative. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.INSTRUCTION_STEP_3: Numbered instruction (step 3 of 4) in the new-device setup flow: wait about 5 minutes while the player boots for the first time. Imperative. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.INSTRUCTION_STEP_4: Numbered instruction (step 4 of 4) in the new-device setup flow: join the Wi-Fi network the user wants the player to use. Imperative. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.CONNECTION_METHOD: Question heading in the new-device setup flow, above the choice between a Wireless (Wi-Fi) and a Wired (Ethernet cable) connection for the player. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.CONNECTION_WIRELESS: Choice button/option in the new-device setup flow: connect the player to the network over Wi-Fi. Adjective used as a short option label. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.CONNECTION_WIRED: Choice button/option in the new-device setup flow: connect the player to the network with an Ethernet cable. Adjective used as a short option label. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.DEVICE_ALREADY_SETUP: Status message in the new-device setup flow: the player found has already been set up, so the search continues for another, not-yet-configured player. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.LOOKING_FOR_WIRELESS_DEVICES: Progress status in the new-device setup flow while scanning for new players reachable over Wi-Fi (players broadcasting their own setup hotspot). No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.LOOKING_FOR_WIRED_DEVICES: Progress status in the new-device setup flow while scanning the local network for new players connected by Ethernet cable. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.CONNECTED_TO_WIRELESS: Status fragment in the new-device setup flow, likely followed by the Wi-Fi network or device name: the connection succeeded (past state). No render site found; keep it a lead-in to a name.
DEVICESETUP.CONNECTING_TO_WIRELESS: Status fragment in the new-device setup flow, likely followed by the Wi-Fi network or device name: connection in progress. No render site found; keep it a lead-in to a name.
DEVICESETUP.DEVICE_CONNECTION_METHOD: Question heading in the new-device setup flow, above the choice between a Wi-Fi and an Ethernet-cable connection for the player (variant of the CONNECTION_METHOD question). No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.OR_SELECT_WIRELESS_NETWORK: Heading above a list of other Wi-Fi networks in the new-device setup flow, offered as an alternative to the suggested network. Verb: pick one. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.SELECT_WIRELESS_NETWORK: Heading/instruction in the new-device setup flow above the list of Wi-Fi networks the player can join. Verb: pick one. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.DEVICE_FOUND: Status/title in the new-device setup flow when a new, not-yet-configured player has been detected. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.SKIP_WIFI: Button/option in the new-device setup flow to skip Wi-Fi setup and keep the player on its Ethernet cable connection only. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ENTER_WIFI_PASSWORD: Prompt fragment in the new-device setup flow, likely followed by the Wi-Fi network name: asks for that network's password. No render site found; keep it a lead-in to a name.
DEVICESETUP.CHECKING_UPDATES: Progress status in the new-device setup flow while the player checks online for a newer system software version. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.WAIT_FEW_MINUTES: Secondary line under a progress status in the new-device setup flow, warning the step may last a few minutes. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.WAIT_5_MINUTES: Secondary line under a progress status in the new-device setup flow (e.g. software update or restart): may take up to 5 minutes, asks the user to wait. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.WAIT_30_SECONDS: Secondary line under a progress status in the new-device setup flow: may take up to 30 seconds, asks the user to wait. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.REBOOTING_DEVICE: Progress status in the new-device setup flow while the player reboots (restarts) itself. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.UPDATING_DEVICE: Progress status in the new-device setup flow while the player installs the newest system software version. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.DEVICE_UP_TO_DATE: Status/result in the new-device setup flow: the player already runs the latest system software, no update needed. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.GRANT_PERMISSIONS: Instruction in the new-device setup flow (phone app): when the phone shows a system permission request (e.g. Wi-Fi/local network/location), allow it so the app can reach the player. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.DEFAULT_NETWORK: Label above the Wi-Fi network the phone is currently using, suggested as the network for the player in the new-device setup flow. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.OTHER_NETWORKS: Heading above the list of other Wi-Fi networks in the new-device setup flow, as an alternative to the user's current network. Verb: pick one. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_NO_WIRELESS_DEVICE_FOU: Error title in the new-device setup flow: no new player was detected over Wi-Fi. 'We' = the app. No render site found.
Error body under 'could not find a wireless device' in the setup flow; the quoted names must match the button labels Retry, Manual setup (MANUAL_WIFI_SELECTION) and Wired setup. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_WIRELESS_DEVICE_CONNEC: Error title in the new-device setup flow: the app found the player but could not connect to it over Wi-Fi. No render site found.
Error body under the Wi-Fi connection failure title in the new-device setup flow: retry, or connect the player with an Ethernet cable instead. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_NO_WIRED_DEVICES_FOUND: Error title in the new-device setup flow: no new player was found on the local network via Ethernet cable. No render site found.
Error body under 'No wired devices found' in the new-device setup flow: check the player is switched on and its cable gives it internet access. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_COULD_NOT_CONNECT_TO_W: Error title fragment in the new-device setup flow, likely followed by the Wi-Fi network name: the player failed to join that network. No render site found; keep it a lead-in to a name.
Error body under the failed Wi-Fi join in the new-device setup flow: probably a wrong Wi-Fi password; check it or use an Ethernet cable. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_COULD_NOT_UPDATE: Error title in the new-device setup flow: the system software update of the player failed. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.ERROR_COULD_NOT_UPDATE_SUB: Error body under the failed update in the new-device setup flow: run the update later from the player's own web interface (its settings). No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.MANUAL_WIFI_SELECTION: Button in the new-device setup flow to start manual setup (choosing the Wi-Fi/device yourself instead of automatic discovery); referenced by name as 'Manual setup' in ERROR_NO_WIRELESS_DEVICE_FOUND_SUB. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.WIRED_SETUP: Option or heading in the first-run device setup: set up the player connected to the router with an Ethernet cable, instead of over Wi-Fi. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.MANUAL_SETUP: Option or heading in the first-run device setup: connect to the player's own Wi-Fi hotspot by hand from the phone's Wi-Fi list, when automatic discovery fails. No render site found.
DEVICESETUP.MANUAL_SETUP_SUB: Instructions under the manual wireless setup heading. Quoted button names must match the actual buttons; Volumio-XXXXX is the player's hotspot name (X = digits/letters), keep as is. Hotspot is open, no password.
DEVICESETUP.SELECT_NETWORK: Heading or prompt in the first-run device setup, above the list of Wi-Fi networks the player can join; user picks one. No render site found.
COMMON.RETRY: Generic button to repeat an action that failed (e.g. a connection attempt). Verb. No render site found.
COMMON.EXIT: Generic button to leave the current screen, flow or wizard. Verb. No render site found.
COMMON.OK: Generic confirm button in dialogs of the classic web UI (default modal, password prompt, search, updater); closes the dialog accepting it. Keep very short.
COMMON.PASSWORD: Generic label for a password input field (e.g. Wi-Fi or network share password). Noun. No render site found.
COMMON.NEW: Button in the classic web UI Add to Playlist dialog: create a new playlist with the typed name. Short button, adjective used as action (new playlist).
COMMON.OPEN_DEVICE: Button that opens the player's own web interface (navigates to the Volumio device). No render site found.
COMMON.PROGRESS: Generic label for a progress indicator (e.g. update or install progress). Noun. No render site found.
COMMON.CONNECT: Generic button to connect, e.g. to a Wi-Fi network or a device. Verb. No render site found.
COMMON.CONTINUE: Button in the warning dialog shown before saving a static IP on the Network settings page (wired or Wi-Fi); confirms and applies the settings. Paired with Cancel.
COMMON.SAVE: Save button at the bottom of a settings section (e.g. Playback Options: output device, DSP, playback); also in classic UI dialogs (web radio edit, alarm clock). Verb, short button.
COMMON.YES: Confirm button in the generic Yes/No confirmation dialog of the classic web UI; accepts the question asked in the dialog body.
COMMON.NO: Decline button in the generic Yes/No confirmation dialog of the classic web UI; closes the dialog without doing the action.
COMMON.GOT_IT: Single acknowledge button closing an informational dialog (e.g. music library scan in progress, no audio output device found). Means 'understood', dismisses the dialog.
COMMON.CANCEL: Cancel button in system dialogs, e.g. the static IP warning on the Network settings page; closes the dialog without applying anything. Verb.
COMMON.RESTART_SYSTEM: Button in the classic web UI system update dialog, shown after a successful update; reboots the player to finish installing it. Verb phrase.
COMMON.TRY_AGAIN: Generic button to retry an action that failed. Verb phrase. No render site found.
COMMON.DELETE: Button in the classic web UI Alarm Clock dialog that removes that alarm. Verb.
COMMON.ADD: Button in classic web UI dialogs (add web radio station, alarm clock) that adds the new item. Verb, short button.
COMMON.POWER_OFF: Button in the classic web UI power menu (and in the terms-of-service decline dialog) that shuts the player down completely. Verb phrase.
COMMON.REBOOT_SYSTEM: Button in the classic web UI power menu that reboots the player (turn off and on again). Verb, sits next to Power Off.
COMMON.ACTION: Field heading in the classic web UI Sleep timer dialog, above a dropdown choosing what happens when the timer ends (e.g. stop music or power off). Noun.
COMMON.ACTIVE: Status text: in the plugin list shows a plugin is running (opposite Inactive); in the Sleep timer dialog, heading of the on/off switch enabling the timer. Adjective.
COMMON.INACTIVE: Status text next to a dot in the classic web UI plugin list: the plugin is installed but not running. Adjective, opposite of Active.
COMMON.SHOW_SETTINGS: Tooltip on the classic web UI menu (hamburger) button that opens the settings side menu; also text under a plugin to reveal its settings. Verb phrase.
COMMON.SETTINGS: Button (and its tooltip) on a plugin row in the classic web UI plugin list; opens that plugin's settings page. Noun, short button.
COMMON.TAB_BROWSE: Main navigation tab/button (and tooltip) in the classic web UI that opens the music browser (sources, library, playlists). Noun/verb as a section name; keep short.
COMMON.TAB_HOME: Main navigation tab in the web UI that opens the home screen. Section name, keep short. No render site found.
COMMON.TAB_SEARCH: Tab-bar button label and tooltip in the classic web UI that opens the music search screen. Section name, keep very short.
COMMON.TAB_SETTINGS: Tab-bar button label and tooltip in the classic web UI that opens the settings menu. Section name, keep very short.
COMMON.TAB_PLAYBACK: Tab-bar button label, tooltip and icon alt text in the classic web UI opening the Now Playing screen (current track and controls). Section name, short.
COMMON.TAB_QUEUE: Tab-bar button label, tooltip and icon alt text in the classic web UI opening the play queue (list of upcoming tracks). Noun, short.
COMMON.TAB_OUTPUTS: Tab-bar button in the classic web UI playback screen that opens the list of audio outputs/players (multiroom groups). Noun, plural, short label.
COMMON.TAB_VOLUME: Tooltip on a volume control in the classic web UI outputs list; followed by a space and the current volume number (e.g. 'Volume 45'). Noun.
COMMON.ARTIST: Label of the artist field (CD ripper dialog, track info) and, in search results, singular word in a heading built as 'Found' + count + this word (used when count is 1). Noun, singular.
COMMON.ARTISTS: Name of the Artists category in the music library browser; also plural word in search result headings ('Found' + count + this word). Noun, plural.
COMMON.ALBUM: Label of the album field (CD ripper dialog, track info) and, in search results, singular word in a heading built as 'Found' + count + this word (count is 1). Noun, singular.
COMMON.ALBUMS: Name of a music-library browse category (folder) listing all albums, shown in the Browse section next to Artists, Genres and Playlists. Noun, plural.
COMMON.SONG: Hover tooltip on the current track title in the classic web UI's now-playing info; labels the field as the song/track being played. Noun, singular.
COMMON.SONGS: Column header in the My Music statistics table (next to Artists, Albums) and section heading listing the tracks in the CD ripper dialog. Noun, plural: songs/tracks.
COMMON.PLAYTIME: Column header in the My Music statistics table on wider screens: total playing duration of the library. On phones the shorter 'Time' header replaces it.
COMMON.TIME: Short column header for total playing duration in the My Music statistics table, used only on phone-width screens instead of 'Playtime'. Keep very short.
COMMON.RESCAN: Button with a refresh icon on the Network Drives page and in the wizard's music step, shown while adding a drive; searches the network again for shares/NAS devices. Verb.
COMMON.SYSTEM_VERSION: Panel title on the System settings page and the label before the installed Volumio OS version number (code appends ': ' and the version).
COMMON.RELEASED: Label on the System Version panel, followed by ': ' and the build date of the installed OS version. Means release/build date, past participle.
COMMON.CLOSE: Button in dialogs pushed by the plugin manager (after a plugin install, or on an install/update error) that dismisses the dialog. Verb.
COMMON.MY_MUSIC: Title of toasts about the music library database scan (scan started, scan error); refers to the user's own local music collection section 'My Music'.
COMMON.SEARCH: Placeholder and tooltip of the search field in the Browse section of the classic web UI; searches the music library and services. Verb/noun as field hint.
COMMON.FAVOURITES: Name of the browse folder/playlist holding tracks and web radios the user marked as favorites (heart). Noun, plural; shown in Browse sources and playlist titles.
COMMON.NAME: Field label and placeholder in the dialog for adding/editing a web radio station; the station's display name. Noun.
COMMON.URL: Field label and placeholder in the add/edit web radio dialog for the stream's web address (URL). Keep as the technical term for a web address.
COMMON.BACK: Tooltip on the back-arrow button when browsing the music library, and back button in MyVolumio terms and referral screens; returns to the previous level/screen. Verb.
COMMON.OPTIONS: Tooltip on the three-dot menu button on a browse list row; code appends ' ...'. Opens the item's options menu (Play, Add to queue, etc.). Noun, plural.
COMMON.CHOOSE_PLAYLIST: Placeholder of the playlist picker in the alarm clock dialog (side menu): the user selects which playlist the alarm will play. Imperative.
COMMON.STOP_MUSIC: Tooltip on the Stop button among the player transport controls in the classic web UI; stops playback. Imperative verb phrase.
COMMON.HOME: Tooltip on the house-icon button in Browse and main menu; returns to the top level of the music library browse view (start page). Noun used as navigation.
COMMON.VOLUME_MUTE: Tooltip on the speaker-off button in the volume control; toggles muting the audio output. Verb (action).
COMMON.VOLUME_MUTED: Status text shown above the volume knob/number when audio is muted. Adjective/state, not a button.
COMMON.VOLUME_UP: Tooltip on the volume-plus button in the volume control; raises the volume one step.
COMMON.VOLUME_DOWN: Tooltip on the volume-minus button in the volume control; lowers the volume one step.
COMMON.HIDDEN: Checkbox label on the Wi-Fi settings page, when connecting manually: marks the network as a hidden Wi-Fi (one that does not broadcast its name/SSID). Adjective.
COMMON.LIST: Tooltip on the view-toggle button in Browse while the grid view is active; switches the music library to list view. Noun (view mode), pairs with 'Grid'.
COMMON.PLAY_QUEUE: Tooltip on the footer navigation button that opens the play queue: the ordered list of tracks waiting to be played. Noun.
COMMON.ENTER_PASSWORD: Title of the password prompt dialog in the classic web UI (e.g. for a protected setting or Wi-Fi). Imperative.
COMMON.INVALID_PASSWORD: Error message shown under the password prompt dialog when the entered password is wrong.
COMMON.RIP: Tooltip on the download-icon button when browsing an audio CD, and the confirm button in the CD ripper dialog; copies the CD tracks to local storage (CD ripping). Verb, not 'rest in peace'.
COMMON.SKIP: No render site found; generic button to skip a step (e.g. in setup/wizard flows) and move on without doing it. Verb.
COMMON.NEXT: Button in the first-run wizard's bottom bar and in the guided UI tour; goes to the next step. Verb/adverb, keep short.
COMMON.PREVIOUS: Button in the first-run wizard's bottom bar and in the guided UI tour; goes back to the previous step. Keep short.
COMMON.DONE: Button on the last step of the first-run wizard and the guided UI tour, and closing the audio outputs panel; finishes and closes. Keep short.
COMMON.EMAIL: Placeholder of the email address field in the wizard step where the user can subscribe to the Volumio newsletter. Noun.
COMMON.SUBSCRIBE_ME: Submit button in the wizard's newsletter step; signs the entered email address up to the Volumio mailing list. First-person imperative.
COMMON.SHARE: No render site found; generic action button to share an item (verb, as in share a link), not a network share/folder.
COMMON.EJECT: Tooltip on the eject-icon button shown when browsing an inserted CD or removable drive; ejects/unmounts the media. Verb.
COMMON.FUNCTIONALIES_CONTROL: Panel title on the My Music settings page above a list of on/off toggles that enable or disable music-library features (plugins). Noun phrase: feature controls.
COMMON.UPDATE_ALBUMART: Button in the CD ripper dialog that fetches/refreshes the cover image (album art) for the CD being ripped. Verb phrase.
COMMON.YEAR: Field label in the CD ripper dialog for the album's release year. Noun; narrow label column.
COMMON.GENRE: Field label in the CD ripper dialog of the classic web UI, next to an editable text box holding the music genre of the album being ripped (copied from CD). Noun, singular.
COMMON.EDIT: Button with a gear icon on the MyVolumio profile page of the classic web UI, next to the user's name; opens profile editing. Verb. Hidden on small screens.
COMMON.GRID: Tooltip of the view toggle button in the music browser of the classic web UI: switches the list of items to a grid of cover tiles. Alternates with 'List'. Noun (grid layout).
COMMON.REMOVE: Button in the audio outputs panel of the classic web UI, under a playback device (e.g. a multiroom speaker) that is in use: removes that device from the current playback. Verb.
COMMON.DSP: Label and tooltip of a button in the audio outputs panel of the classic web UI that opens the DSP (digital sound processing: equalizer, filters) settings. Technical abbreviation.
COMMON.DISABLE: Button (and its tooltip) in a popup of the audio outputs panel of the classic web UI: stops playing on this device's local output; the other choice is to continue playing. Verb.
COMMON.ACCEPT: Button in the MyVolumio Terms of Service dialog of the classic web UI: agrees to the terms. Pairs with 'Decline'. Verb.
COMMON.DECLINE: Button in the MyVolumio Terms of Service dialog of the classic web UI: refuses the terms. Pairs with 'Accept'. Verb.
COMMON.ACCEPT_OR_SHUTDOWN: Body of the Terms of Service dialog in the classic web UI, shown after the user declined: the system can only be used if the terms are accepted; otherwise turn the device off.
COMMON.RELATED: Word joined in code with a space and 'Artists' or 'Albums' to form a section title in the classic web UI's artist/album page (e.g. 'Related Artists'). Adjective: similar or connected to the current one.
COMMON.INSTANT_PLAY: Button beside 'Search' in the classic web UI's smart search box: starts playing the best result right away without showing the list. Idiom; neutral meaning: just play the top match.
COMMON.SUPER_SEARCH: Placeholder and tooltip of the search field in the classic web UI for the smart search that understands free-form requests across music sources. Feature name.
COMMON.SUPER_SEARCH_EXAMPLE: Hint under or inside the smart search box of the classic web UI showing a sample free-form request the user can type. Keep the example query natural. No render site found.
COMMON.ADD_QUEUE_TEXT_1: Fragment of a success toast after adding music to the play queue; code puts the file or item name right before it (no space added), so keep the trailing space. Paired with ' to queue' in some flows.
COMMON.ADD_QUEUE_TEXT_2: Closing fragment of the 'Added <item> to queue' toast; follows the item name, keep the leading space. 'Queue' = the list of tracks waiting to play. No render site found.
COMMON.ADD_QUEUE_TITLE: Title of a success toast after the user adds a track, album or playlist to the play queue (list of upcoming tracks); the message is the item's name. Also usable as a menu action.
COMMON.CANNOT_LIST: Start of an error message when browsing fails; code appends a space and the section name, e.g. 'My Web Radios' or 'Favourites'. Means the items could not be loaded/shown.
COMMON.CONFIGURATION_UPDATE: Generic toast title after a settings change is saved (e.g. browse sources visibility, playback config); the message tells what changed or that an error occurred.
COMMON.CONFIGURATION_UPDATE_DESCRIPTION: Generic toast message confirming that settings were saved successfully, under the 'Configuration update' title. No render site found.
COMMON.CONFIGURATION_UPDATE_ERROR: Message of an error toast titled 'Configuration update', shown when saving playback/audio settings fails. Generic error sentence.
COMMON.CONNECTED: Toast message fragment titled 'My Music': code puts the drive's name and a space before it, announcing that a USB or internal drive was plugged in and is ready. Adjective, refers to the drive.
COMMON.DISABLED: Shared adjective: toast title when a music source plugin is turned off (message = plugin name); status of Infinity Play; and the 'off' option of the default startup volume dropdown in Playback Options.
COMMON.DISCONNECTED: Toast message fragment titled 'My Music': code puts the drive's name and a space before it, announcing that a USB or internal drive was removed. Adjective, refers to the drive.
COMMON.ENABLED: Shared adjective: toast title when a music source plugin is turned on (message = plugin name); also the status shown in the Infinity Play toast. Means switched on/active.
COMMON.ERROR: Generic error toast title (failed UI switch, network drive errors); also appended after a space to a plugin operation name to form a dialog title, e.g. '<Install> Error'. Noun.
COMMON.FOUND: Start of a search results heading in the music library; code appends ' <count> <artists/albums/tracks>' then " '<search text>'". Past-tense verb: the search found that many.
COMMON.GENRES: Name of a browse category in the music library (alongside Artists and Albums) that lists music by genre. Plural noun, used as a menu/tile title.
COMMON.ILLEGAL_CHARACTER_/: Warning toast (title 'My Music') when adding a network drive: the name typed contains a slash '/', which is not allowed. Ask the user to delete that character; keep the '/' literal.
COMMON.LAST_100: Name of a browse category in the music library listing the 100 most recently played tracks (play history). Short tile/menu title.
COMMON.LOGGING_IN: Progress status while signing in to a MyVolumio account (cloud account). Ongoing action. No render site found.
COMMON.LOGGING_OUT: Progress status while signing out of a MyVolumio account (cloud account). Ongoing action. No render site found.
COMMON.LOGIN: Button in a dialog shown when a plugin needs a MyVolumio account: opens the MyVolumio sign-in page. Next to 'Close'. Means 'sign in' (verb).
COMMON.LOGIN_FAIL: Error message when signing in to a MyVolumio account fails; lowercase, may be appended to another word or name. No render site found.
COMMON.LOGIN_SUCCESS: Confirmation message after signing in to a MyVolumio account succeeds. No render site found.
COMMON.LOGOUT: Button or menu entry to sign out of the MyVolumio account (cloud account). Means 'sign out' (verb). No render site found.
COMMON.LOGOUT_SUCCESS: Confirmation message after signing out of a MyVolumio account. No render site found.
COMMON.MATCHING: Lowercase fragment for search result headings, between a count/type and the search text, as in 'N tracks matching <text>'. No render site found; inferred from sibling 'Found'.
COMMON.MEDIA_SERVERS: Name of a browse source in the music library listing DLNA/UPnP media servers found on the home network (e.g. a NAS sharing music). Plural noun, tile/menu title.
COMMON.MUSIC_LIBRARY: Name of the browse source that holds the user's own music files (USB drives, network drives, internal storage), shown as a tile/menu title in Browse.
COMMON.NONE: Option in Playback Options > Volume: the mixer type dropdown value meaning no volume control on the device (volume left to the amplifier/DAC). Also the selected value when none is set.
COMMON.NO_RESULTS: Heading shown in place of results when a music search finds nothing; also an error toast title when an artist/album lookup in the local library finds no match.
COMMON.OFF: Toast message after toggling Random (shuffle) playback, under the title 'Random': means the mode is now disabled. Adjective state, not the verb 'turn off'.
COMMON.ON: Toast message after toggling Random (shuffle) or Repeat playback, under the title 'Random'/'Repeat': means the mode is now enabled. Adjective state.
COMMON.OR: Lowercase conjunction joining two alternatives in a sentence or between two options/buttons (e.g. one choice 'or' another). No render site found.
COMMON.PLAYER_RESTARTED: Toast message (title 'Configuration update') after changing playback settings: the audio playback engine (MPD) was restarted to apply them and is running again.
COMMON.PLAYLISTS: Name of the Playlists folder/source in the Browse music screen; opens the user's saved playlists. Plural noun.
COMMON.PLAY_TEXT: Toast message fragment, currently disabled in code: followed directly by the track name (keep the trailing space), under the title 'Play'.
COMMON.PLAY_TITLE: Toast title shown when playback of a track starts (currently disabled in code). Verb/action label: playback started.
COMMON.REMOVE_FAIL: Error toast message (title 'Error') when deleting an item from a playlist, favorites or the library fails; generic 'the item could not be removed'.
COMMON.REMOVE_QUEUE_TEXT_1: Toast message fragment when a track is removed from the play queue: followed directly by the track name, then ' from queue'. Keep the trailing space.
COMMON.REMOVE_QUEUE_TEXT_2: Toast message fragment: appended directly after 'Remove ' + the track name when a track is removed from the play queue. Keep the leading space.
COMMON.REMOVE_QUEUE_TITLE: Toast title shown when a track is removed from the play queue; the message below names the track. Verb, action that just happened.
COMMON.RESCAN_DB: Toast message (title 'My Music') when a full rescan starts: the music library index is being rebuilt from scratch from all music files.
COMMON.RESTART: Button in a dialog asking to reboot the whole device (e.g. after activating a DAC or DSP program); tap restarts the device. Verb.
COMMON.SAVE_QUEUE_ERROR: Toast when saving the current play queue as a playlist fails; the playlist name is appended directly with no space, so end-punctuation/spacing matters.
COMMON.SAVE_QUEUE_SUCCESS: Toast when the current play queue was saved as a playlist; the playlist name is appended directly with no space or colon.
COMMON.SCAN_DB: Toast message (title 'My Music') and dialog title while the music library index is updated with new/changed files on local or network storage. Ongoing action.
COMMON.SCAN_DB_ERROR: Error toast message (title 'My Music') when the music library scan fails; the technical error text is appended directly after it with no separator.
COMMON.SEARCH_ALBUM_SECTION: Section heading in music search results grouping the matching albums. No render site found.
COMMON.SEARCH_ARTIST_SECTION: Section heading in music search results grouping the matching artists. No render site found.
COMMON.SEARCH_SONG_SECTION: Section heading in music search results grouping the matching tracks (songs). No render site found.
COMMON.SETTINGS_SAVED_SUCCESSFULLY: Generic success toast message after saving a settings section (e.g. Album Art, Playback Options, Network); toast title names the section.
COMMON.SETTINGS_SAVE_ERROR: Generic error toast message (title e.g. 'Playback Options') when applying changed settings failed.
COMMON.SOURCES: Main menu entry and settings page title for music sources: local library, USB/internal storage and network drives (NAS). Plural noun.
COMMON.TRACK: Singular noun used in a search results heading: 'Found' + count + this word + the quoted search term, when exactly one track (song) matched.
COMMON.TRACKS: Plural noun 'songs': in a search results heading ('Found' + count + this word + quoted term) and as a list title followed by ' (' + name + ')'.
COMMON.UPDATING_MUSIC_DB_WAIT_MESSAGE: Dialog body (title 'Updating Music Database', button 'Got it') while the music library is indexed; 'icon on bottom left' is a spinner in the web UI.
COMMON.USERNAME: Field label for an account/login user name (e.g. for a network share or service sign-in). No render site found.
COMMON.WITH: Lowercase preposition joined into a sentence between two values (e.g. one item 'with' another). No render site found.
COMMON.PLEASE_WAIT: Appended to a first-run wizard status: 'Connecting to' + Wi-Fi network name + '... ' then this text, while the device joins the network.
COMMON.SEARCH_RESULTS_TITLE: Setting label: how many search results to show per category in music search. No render site found.
COMMON.ARTIST_NOT_FOUND_IN_YOUR_LIBRARY: Error toast message (title 'No results') when tapping an artist name to open it, but that artist is not in the local music library.
COMMON.ALBUM_NOT_FOUND_IN_YOUR_LIBRARY: Error toast message (title 'No results') when tapping an album name to open it, but that album is not in the local music library.
COMMON.SEARCH_RESULTS_DESC: Help text under the search results setting: the number of results the user wants music search to return. No render site found.
COMMON.MINUTE: Singular time unit, likely after a number (e.g. sleep timer or alarm duration of 1 minute). No render site found.
COMMON.MINUTES: Plural time unit after a number (e.g. sleep timer or alarm duration). No render site found.
COMMON.HOUR: Singular time unit after a number (e.g. sleep timer duration of 1 hour). No render site found.
COMMON.HOURS: Plural time unit after a number (e.g. sleep timer duration). No render site found.
COMMON.SORT_BY: Label on the sort dropdown button in the Browse music screen, followed by a space and the currently selected sort order (e.g. Artist). Keep short.
COMMON.LOGIN_OAUTH: Message in a sign-in dialog with a QR code, when linking a streaming service: scan with phone, sign in to that service's account to allow the device to use it.
COMMON.LOGIN_OAUTH_NOT_POSSIBLE: Dialog message in the classic web UI when signing in to a streaming service plugin can't happen here (no QR code could be made); tells the user to authorize the service from the Volumio mobile app instead.
COMMON.STANDBY: Button in the classic web UI power-off dialog, next to shut down and restart; puts the device into standby (low-power idle) instead of turning it off.
COMMON.FILTER_ALL: Value shown on a filter dropdown button when browsing music, after the filter name and a colon (e.g. 'Genre: All'); means no filter value is selected, everything is shown.
COMMON.PLAY_NEXT_TITLE: Success toast title after the user chooses to play an item next; the toast message is the track or album name that was inserted right after the current track in the queue.
COMMON.CHECK_IF_YOUR_DEVICE_IS_CONNECTED: Error message hint appended after 'Failed to list BBC Radios: ' when the web radio list can't load; asks the user to check the device's internet connection.
COMMON.SHOW_MORE: Browse list entry (with a plus icon) at the end of a UPnP/DLNA media server folder listing; opening it loads the next page of items in that folder.
DEVICELIST.SETUP_NEW_DEVICE: Button or link on the device list screen of the controller app; starts setup of a new Volumio device that isn't configured yet. No render site found.
DEVICELIST.SELECT_A_DEVICE: Title or prompt on the device list screen; asks the user to pick which Volumio device on the network to control. No render site found.
DEVICELIST.SEARCHING_DEVICES: Status text on the device list screen while the app scans the local network for Volumio devices. No render site found.
DEVICELIST.BACK_BUTTON: Hint on the device list/controller screen: pressing the phone's Back button twice returns to the device list to choose another Volumio device. No render site found.
DEVICELIST.NO_DEVICE_FOUND_SETTINGS: Hint on the device list screen when no device is found; 'pressing here' is a tappable link that opens the phone's Local Network privacy permission (iOS) for the app.
UI_SETTINGS.THEME_SETTINGS: Panel title on the classic web UI appearance settings page, heading the background image and color options.
UI_SETTINGS.UPLOAD_BACKGROUND: Heading or button on the classic web UI theme settings panel for uploading your own background image. No render site found.
UI_SETTINGS.UPLOAD_BACKGROUND_FILE: Instruction text above the upload area on the theme settings panel: click to choose an image file, or drag and drop it onto the area, to add a new background.
UI_SETTINGS.UPLOAD_PROGRESS: Label shown while a background image uploads on the theme settings panel; followed by the upload percentage. No render site found.
UI_SETTINGS.SELECT_BACKGROUND: Section heading on the classic web UI theme settings panel, above the gallery of background images to choose from.
UI_SETTINGS.SELECT_BACKGROUND_COLOR: Section heading on the classic web UI theme settings panel, above the color picker for a plain background color.
UI_SETTINGS.APPLY_BACKGROUND: Button on the theme settings panel; sets the selected image as the web UI background.
UI_SETTINGS.APPLY_BACKGROUND_COLOR: Button on the theme settings panel; sets the chosen plain color as the web UI background.
UI_SETTINGS.DELETE_BACKGROUND: Button on the theme settings panel; removes the selected (uploaded) background image from the gallery.
BROWSER.PLAY: Button/menu entry (verb) in the classic web UI: in a browse item's action menu it plays that item; on the player controls it starts playback.
BROWSER.ADD_TO_QUEUE: Menu entry (verb) in a browse item's or album's action menu; appends the track/album to the end of the play queue without interrupting playback.
BROWSER.ADD_TO_PLAYLIST: Menu entry (verb) in a browse item's or album's action menu; opens a picker to add the item to one of the user's saved playlists.
BROWSER.REMOVE_FROM_PLAYLIST: Menu entry (verb) in the action menu of a track inside a saved playlist; removes that track from the playlist.
BROWSER.ADD_TO_FAVOURITES: Menu entry or heart-button tooltip (verb); marks the track/album as a favorite so it appears in the Favorites list.
BROWSER.REMOVE_FROM_FAVOURITES: Menu entry or heart-button tooltip (verb); removes the track/album from the user's Favorites list.
BROWSER.ADD_WEBRADIO: Menu entry (verb) in the browse action menu of the web radio section; opens the dialog to add a custom internet radio station by URL.
BROWSER.EDIT_WEBRADIO: Menu entry (verb) in the action menu of a user-added web radio station; opens the dialog to change its name or stream URL.
BROWSER.DELETE_WEBRADIO: Menu entry (verb) in the action menu of a user-added web radio station; deletes that station from My Web Radios.
BROWSER.ADD_TO_RADIO_FAVOURITES: Menu entry (verb) in a web radio station's action menu; adds the station to the Favorite Radios list.
BROWSER.REMOVE_FROM_RADIO_FAVOURITES: Menu entry (verb) in a web radio station's action menu; removes the station from the Favorite Radios list.
BROWSER.ADD_WEBRADIO_TITLE: Dialog title in the classic web UI for adding a custom internet radio station (name and stream URL fields).
BROWSER.URL_DOC: Help text under the URL field of the Add Web Radio dialog; the address may be a direct audio stream or a link to an M3U or PLS playlist file hosted online.
BROWSER.DELETE_PLAYLIST: Menu entry (verb) in a saved playlist's action menu; deletes the whole playlist.
BROWSER.GO_TO_SHARE: Tooltip on the track actions button on the playback screen; opens a menu to go to the track's artist/album or share it ('Share' is the verb). Keep the dash format compact.
BROWSER.NEXT_TRACK: Tooltip/accessible label of the skip-forward button on the player controls; jumps to the next track in the queue.
BROWSER.PREVIOUS_TRACK: Tooltip/accessible label of the skip-back button on the player controls; goes to the previous track (or restarts the current one).
BROWSER.PAUSE: Tooltip/accessible label of the pause button (verb) on the player controls; pauses playback.
BROWSER.CLEAR_AND_PLAY: Menu entry (verb) in a browse item's action menu; empties the current queue, adds this item and starts playing it.
BROWSER.SAFE_REMOVE: Menu entry (verb) on a USB drive in the browse list; safely unmounts (ejects) the removable drive so it can be unplugged without data loss.
BROWSER.UPDATE_FOLDER: Menu entry (and tooltip) in the item menu of a folder in Browse, classic web UI. 'Update' is a verb: rescans this folder and refreshes its entries in the music library.
BROWSER.DELETE_FOLDER: Menu entry in the item menu of a folder in Browse, classic web UI. Verb: deletes this folder from the device storage.
BROWSER.SKIP_BACKWARDS: Tooltip/label of the player control button that jumps back a few seconds within the current track (classic web UI player bar). Not 'previous track'.
BROWSER.SKIP_FORWARD: Tooltip/label of the player control button that jumps forward a few seconds within the current track (classic web UI player bar). Not 'next track'.
BROWSER.CREDITS: Short heading or label for the credits of a track or album (performers, composers, producers). No render site found; sibling of 'Album credits'. Noun.
BROWSER.ALBUM_CREDITS: Button and section heading on the album page and in the track actions dialog, classic web UI; opens the list of people credited on the album (performers, composers, producers). Noun.
BROWSER.ALBUM_STORY: Button and section heading on the album page and in the track actions dialog, classic web UI; opens a short text about the album's background and history.
BROWSER.TRACK_STORY: Section heading in the track actions dialog, classic web UI; opens a short text about the song's background and history.
BROWSER.ARTIST_STORY: Button and section heading on the album/artist page and in the track actions dialog, classic web UI; opens a short biography of the artist.
BROWSER.READ_MORE: Link under the truncated album or artist description on the album/artist page, classic web UI; expands or opens the full text.
BROWSER.NO_ITEMS: Empty-state heading shown in a Browse list or grid when the folder or source contains nothing, classic web UI.
BROWSER.NOT_FOUND: Short status in the track actions dialog shown in place of album credits, album story or artist story when no information could be found. Keep short.
BROWSER.CREDITS_NOT_FOUND: Message in the credits details dialog, classic web UI, shown when no credits (performers, composers, producers) are available for the item.
BROWSER.ARTIST_STORY_NOT_FOUND_FOR: Fragment shown as a heading in the artist story dialog; code appends a space, the artist name and a period. Means no biography was found for that artist.
BROWSER.RELATED: Section heading listing recommended albums or artists similar to the one being viewed. No render site found; sibling of Related albums/Related Artists.
BROWSER.RELATED_ALBUMS: Section heading on the album page, classic web UI, above a row of similar albums suggested to the user.
BROWSER.RELATED_ARTISTS: Section heading on the artist page, classic web UI, above a row of similar artists suggested to the user.
BROWSER.SUPER_SEARCH: Title of the SuperSearch info dialog, classic web UI. 'Volumio SuperSearch' is the feature name; BETA marks it as an early, test-phase feature.
BROWSER.SUPER_SEARCH_INFO: Body of the SuperSearch info dialog: explains natural-language music search, examples, Autoplay. Contains HTML (br, ul, li); keep tags. TIDAL, QOBUZ, Spotify are brand names.
BROWSER.SUPER_SEARCH_WAIT: Waiting message shown in Browse while a SuperSearch query (natural-language music search) runs, classic web UI.
BROWSER.PLAY_NEXT: Menu entry and button in Browse and on the album page, classic web UI: inserts the item in the queue right after the track now playing. Verb phrase.
MY_MUSIC.UPDATE: Button on the My Music settings page, classic web UI. Verb: updates the music library database for changed, new or deleted files only (quicker than Rescan).
MY_MUSIC.UPDATE_DOC: Help text next to the Update button on the My Music settings page: an incremental refresh of the music library database.
MY_MUSIC.RESCAN: Button on the My Music settings page, classic web UI. Verb: rebuilds the music library database from scratch by scanning every file again.
MY_MUSIC.RESCAN_DOC: Help text next to the Rescan button on the My Music settings page: the whole music library database is rebuilt from all files.
PLUGINS.BACK_TO_PLUGINS: Back link/button returning to the Plugins page from a plugin's settings page. No render site found.
PLUGINS.PLUGINS: Page title of the Plugins page (add-ons that extend Volumio), classic web UI. Noun, plural.
PLUGINS.PLUGINS_MANAGEMENT: Heading on the Plugins page, classic web UI, above the tabs for searching, installing and managing add-on plugins.
PLUGINS.SHOW_DETAILS: Toggle link in the plugin installation progress dialog; expands the detailed installation log. Leading '+' is a visual expand marker; keep it.
PLUGINS.HIDE_DETAILS: Toggle link in the plugin installation progress dialog; collapses the detailed installation log. Leading '-' is a visual collapse marker; keep it.
PLUGINS.INSTALL: Button on a plugin card in Plugins search (verb: install this plugin); also confirm button of the install dialog and a feature heading on the MyVolumio welcome page.
PLUGINS.UNINSTALL: Red button on an installed plugin card, Plugins page; also confirm button of the uninstall dialog. Verb: removes the plugin from the device.
PLUGINS.UPDATE: Button on a plugin card, Plugins page, shown when a newer version exists. Verb: installs the new version of this plugin.
PLUGINS.DETAILS: Button on a plugin card in Plugins search; opens more information about the plugin (description, version, author).
PLUGINS.DROP: Prompt inside the upload area of the Upload Plugin tab: click to pick a plugin package file, or drag and drop it onto the area.
PLUGINS.INSTALL_PROGRESS: Heading above the progress bar on the Upload Plugin tab while an uploaded plugin is being installed.
PLUGINS.INSTALLED_PLUGINS: Tab title on the Plugins page listing the plugins already installed on the device.
PLUGINS.SEARCH_PLUGINS: Tab title on the Plugins page to browse and search the catalogue of available plugins. 'Search' is a verb.
PLUGINS.UPLOAD_PLUGINS: Tab title on the Plugins page to install a plugin from a package file the user uploads. 'Upload' is a verb. No render site found.
PLUGINS.CHECKING_DEPENDENCIES: Progress status in the plugin installation dialog: the system checks the plugin is compatible with the installed Volumio version.
PLUGINS.CHECKING_DUPLICATE_PLUGIN: Progress step shown in the plugin install dialog (and appended to its detailed log): the system is checking whether this plugin is already installed. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.CONFIRM_PLUGIN_INSTALL: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before installing a plugin from the Plugins page, when install warnings are enabled. Verb phrase: asks the user to confirm installing.
PLUGINS.CONFIRM_PLUGIN_INSTALL_WARNING_M: Body of the confirmation dialog before installing a plugin: warns that community plugins come from third-party developers and may cause problems, then asks to confirm. (English has a typo, 'instabilitiy'.)
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_LOGIN_MESSAGE: Body of the dialog shown when opening the plugin store while not signed in to MyVolumio (the Volumio cloud account). Contains an HTML link <a href=...> around the sign-in phrase; keep the tag and URL intact.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_LOGIN: Title of the dialog shown when opening the plugin store while not signed in to MyVolumio (Volumio cloud account); polite request to sign in. Dialog buttons are Close and Login.
PLUGINS.CONFIRM_PLUGIN_UNINSTALL: Title of the confirmation dialog shown after the user taps Uninstall on a plugin in the Plugins page; asks to confirm removing the plugin.
PLUGINS.CONFIRM_PLUGIN_UNINSTALL_MESSAGE: Body of the confirmation dialog shown after the user taps Uninstall on a plugin; question asking whether to really remove it.
PLUGINS.COPYING_PLUGIN_TO_LOCATION: Progress step in the plugin install dialog and its detailed log: the plugin files are being copied to their install folder on the device. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.CREATING_INSTALL_LOCATION: Progress step in the plugin install/update dialog's detailed log: the system is creating the folder the plugin will be installed into. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.DOWNLOADING: No render site found; likely a progress status or dialog title in the plugin install flow meaning the plugin package is being downloaded. Ongoing action.
PLUGINS.DOWNLOADING_FROM: No render site found; a fragment for the plugin install progress, followed in code by the download URL or source; keep the trailing space before the appended value.
PLUGINS.DOWNLOADING_PLUGIN: First progress message (10%) in the plugin install/update dialog: the plugin package is being downloaded to the device. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.ENABLE_PLUGIN: Button in the dialog shown when a plugin install completes, next to Close; tapping it turns the newly installed plugin on (starts it). Verb, short button label.
PLUGINS.ENABLE_PLUGIN_NOW_QUESTION: Second half of the install-complete message: code builds '<plugin name> Successfully Installed, ' then this question. Asks whether to turn the plugin on now; answered by the Enable Plugin button.
PLUGINS.FINALIZING_INSTALLATION: Progress step (90%) in the plugin install/update dialog and its detailed log: last setup tasks after the install script ran. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.FINALIZING_UNINSTALL: Progress step (90%) in the plugin uninstall dialog: last cleanup after the plugin was removed from the configuration. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.INSTALLING_NECESSARY_UTILITIES: Progress step (70%) in the plugin install/update dialog: the plugin's install script is installing the software packages it depends on. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.INSTALLING_PLUGIN: Title of the plugin install progress dialog (also used while an install waits in the queue). Ongoing action: a plugin is being installed.
PLUGINS.NO_CONFIGURATION_AVAILABLE: Page title shown when opening the settings of a plugin that has no settings page; the page is otherwise empty. Status text.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_DISABLED: Progress step (60%) in the plugin uninstall dialog: the plugin has been switched off before removal. Past-tense status.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_INSTALL_COMPLETED: No render site found; status or dialog title for a finished plugin operation. Note the English says 'update' although the key says install; keep the meaning of the English.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_INSTALL_ERROR_OCCURRED: Error message in the plugin install dialog when installation fails; code appends a space and the technical error text after it.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_START_ERROR: Error toast message when a plugin fails to start; the toast title is '<plugin name> Plugin'. Tells the user to install an updated version or contact the plugin's developer.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_STOPPED: Progress step in the plugin update and uninstall dialogs: the running plugin has been stopped before files are changed. Past-tense status.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UNINSTALLED: Final message (100%) in the plugin uninstall dialog confirming the plugin was removed; shown with a close button. Past-tense status.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UNINSTALL_ERROR_OCCURRED: Error message in the plugin uninstall dialog when removal fails; code appends ': ' and the technical error text after it.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UNINSTALL_FAILED: Title of the plugin uninstall dialog when removal failed (the body carries the error details). Short status headline.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UPDATE_COMPLETED: Title of the plugin update dialog once the update finished successfully (100%). Short status headline.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UPDATE_ERROR_OCCURRED: Error message in the plugin update dialog when the update fails; code appends a space and the technical error text after it.
PLUGINS.PLUGIN_UPDATE_FAILED: Title of the plugin update dialog when the update failed; shown with a Close button and the error details below. Short status headline.
PLUGINS.REMOVING_NECESSARY_UTILITIES: Progress step (70%) in the plugin uninstall dialog: the uninstall script is removing the software packages the plugin had installed. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.SUCCESSFULLY_INSTALLED: Title of the dialog when a plugin install completes; also joined in the message as '<plugin name> ' + this + ', ' + the 'enable now?' question. Past-participle status.
PLUGINS.SUCCESSFULLY_UPDATED_PLUGIN: Final message in the plugin update dialog and its detailed log confirming the plugin was updated. Past-tense status.
PLUGINS.UNINSTALLING_PLUGIN: Title of the plugin uninstall progress dialog; code appends a space and the plugin name after it. Ongoing action.
PLUGINS.UNPACKING_PLUGIN: Progress step (40%) in the plugin install/update dialog: the downloaded plugin archive (zip) is being extracted. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.UPDATING_PLUGIN: Title of the plugin update progress dialog, shown while a plugin is being updated to a newer version. Ongoing action.
PLUGINS.UPDATING_PLUGIN_FILES: Progress step (60%) in the plugin update dialog: the plugin's files on the device are being replaced with the new version. Ongoing action, status text.
PLUGINS.WAITING_FOR_RUNNING_INSTALL: Message in the plugin install dialog when another plugin install is already running: this install is queued and starts automatically afterwards. Dialog title is 'Installing plugin'.
UPDATER.DOWNLOAD_SPEED: Label in the system update progress dialog (classic web UI), under the progress bar; followed by ': ' and the current download speed value. Noun phrase, tight space.
UPDATER.TIME_REMAINING: Label in the system update progress dialog (classic web UI), next to download speed; followed by ': ' and the estimated time left (ETA). Noun phrase, tight space.
UPDATER.UPDATE_NOW: Button in the system update dialog of the classic web UI that starts installing the available software update immediately; also tooltip of the update-notification icon in the top bar. Verb.
UPDATER.UPDATE_AVAILABLE: Notification banner text in the classic web UI top bar/side menu: a new version of the system software can be installed; tapping it opens the update dialog.
UPDATER.CHECKING_FOR_UPDATES: Title of the update dialog while the device checks online for new system software; shown with 'Please Wait' as the description.
UPDATER.CHECKING_FOR_UPDATES_WAIT: Description line in the update dialog under the title 'Checking for Updates', asking the user to wait while the check runs.
UPDATER.CLEANING: Progress status in the system update dialog: the updater is removing old, no-longer-needed files.
UPDATER.CREATING_BACKUP: Progress status in the system update dialog: a backup copy of the current system is being made before updating. Verb in progress.
UPDATER.DOWNLOADING_UPDATE: Progress status in the system update dialog: the new system software is being downloaded.
UPDATER.ERROR: Generic status shown in the system update dialog when the update reports an error. Noun.
UPDATER.ERROR_UPDATE_FAILED: Error status in the system update dialog: the software update failed; restart the device and try the update again.
UPDATER.ERROR_UPDATE_FILE_NOT_FOUND: Error status in the system update dialog: the downloaded update package file could not be found on the device.
UPDATER.FINALIZING_UPDATE: Progress status in the system update dialog: last step of installing the update.
UPDATER.PREPARING_UPDATE: Progress status in the system update dialog: first step, getting ready to install the update.
UPDATER.SUCCESSFULLY_UPDATED_TO_VERSION: Start of the update-complete status: code joins it with a space, the new version number, '. ', then SYSTEM_RESTART_IN. Keep it a lead-in to a version number.
UPDATER.SYSTEM_RESTART_IN: Sentence after the update-complete message ('...to version X. ' + this): the device reboots shortly, likely followed by a countdown; keep the trailing space.
UPDATER.SYSTEM_RESTART_REQUIRED: Message after a system update or setting change asking the user to reboot the device for it to take effect. No render site found.
UPDATER.UPDATE: Short button or title for the system software update (likely a verb on a button: start the update). No render site found.
TRACK_MANAGER.PLAYING: Green label at the left of the classic web UI's bottom track info bar, followed by the current track title; shown only while music plays. Means 'now playing'.
TRACK_MANAGER.BY: Small connector word in the track info bar, between the playing track title and the artist name (a link to the artist). Followed by the artist name.
TRACK_MANAGER.FROM: Small connector word in the track info bar, before the album name (a link to the album) of the playing track. Followed by the album name.
TRACK_MANAGER.GO_TO_ARTIST: Button in the now-playing actions sheet of the classic web UI: opens the browse page of the current track's artist.
TRACK_MANAGER.GO_TO_ALBUM: Button in the now-playing actions sheet of the classic web UI: opens the browse page of the current track's album.
TRACK_MANAGER.TWEET_TRACK: Button with the Twitter/X logo in the now-playing actions sheet: share the current track in a post on Twitter (X). 'Tweet' = post on Twitter, verb.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.RANDOM: Tooltip of the shuffle button in the player controls: play the queue in random order (toggle). Keep short.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.REPEAT: Tooltip of the repeat button in the classic web UI's player controls (toggle: repeat the queue, or a single track). Keep short.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.REPEAT_ALL: Tooltip/label of the repeat button state that repeats the whole queue, in the player controls and the now-playing actions sheet.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.REPEAT_SINGLE: Tooltip/label of the repeat button state that repeats only the current track, in the player controls and the now-playing actions sheet.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.REPEAT_OFF: Tooltip/label of the repeat button state with repeat turned off, in the player controls and the now-playing actions sheet.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.SAVE_QUEUE_AS_PLAYLIST: Tooltip of the save button in the track info bar of the classic web UI: store the current play queue as a new or existing playlist. Verb.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.CONSUME_PLAYLIST: Player mode toggle: each track is removed from the queue after it plays ('consume' = use up). No render site found.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.CLEAR_QUEUE: Tooltip of the button in the track info bar of the classic web UI that removes all tracks from the play queue. Verb.
TRACK_INFO_BAR.INFINITY_PLAY: Name of the feature that keeps playing similar music automatically after the queue ends: button tooltip, onboarding tip title, and toast title (message: Enabled/Disabled).
NETWORKFS.NO_DRIVES_FOUND: Info message on the add network drive form after a scan of the local network finds no NAS/shared folders.
NETWORKFS.ALIAS: Field label on the add/edit network drive form and column header in the network drives list (settings and setup wizard): the display name the user gives the share.
NETWORKFS.ALIAS_DOC: Help text under the Alias field of the network drive form: pick a name shown for this drive in the list of mounted NAS shares; also a warning toast when the name is left blank.
NETWORKFS.NAS_IP_ADDRESS: Field label on the add/edit network drive form: the IP address of the NAS (network storage) holding the music.
NETWORKFS.NAS_IP_ADDRESS_DOC: Help text under the NAS IP Address field of the add/edit network drive form: the numeric network address of the user's network drive.
NETWORKFS.NAS_PATH: Field label on the add/edit network drive form: the shared folder name (or subfolder path) on the NAS. Noun. No render site found for the label.
NETWORKFS.NAS_PATH_DOC: Help text under the Path field of the add/edit network drive form: the name of the network share (shared folder, noun) or a subfolder path inside it.
NETWORKFS.SHARE_TYPE: Field label (select: e.g. CIFS/SMB or NFS) on the add/edit network drive form: the file-sharing protocol the NAS uses. 'Share' is a noun here.
NETWORKFS.USERNAME: Field label and placeholder on the add/edit network drive form: the user name for signing in to the NAS share, if it requires credentials.
NETWORKFS.PASSWORD: Field label in the add/edit network drive form (classic web UI, Sources/My Music settings): password of the user account on the NAS share. Noun.
NETWORKFS.OPTIONS: Field label in the advanced part of the add/edit network drive form: free-text extra mount options for the NAS share (technical, e.g. SMB version). Noun, plural.
NETWORKFS.SHOW_OPTIONS: Button (and tooltip) in the add/edit network drive form that reveals the advanced fields (file system type, user, password, mount options). Verb phrase.
NETWORKFS.HIDE_OPTIONS: Button (and tooltip) in the add/edit network drive form that collapses the advanced fields again. Verb phrase, opposite of Show Advanced Options.
NETWORKFS.NETWORK_DRIVES: Panel title on the Sources (My Music) settings page of the classic web UI: list of NAS shares (SMB/CIFS or NFS) the player reads music from. Noun, plural.
NETWORKFS.ADD_DRIVE: Button (and tooltip) in the Network Drives panel and the first-run wizard music step; opens the form to add a NAS share as a music source. Verb phrase.
NETWORKFS.NAME: Field label for the display name (alias) the user gives to a network drive (NAS share). Noun. No render site found.
NETWORKFS.PATH: Field label in the add/edit network drive form and column header in the drives list: folder path of the share on the NAS. Noun.
NETWORKFS.MOUNTED: Column header in the network drives list (settings and wizard): whether the NAS share is currently connected and readable by the player. Status adjective.
NETWORKFS.SIZE: Column header in the network drives list (settings and wizard): storage size of the NAS share. Noun.
NETWORKFS.SCANNING_FOR_NETWORK_DRIVES: Status message with a spinner in the add network drive form, shown while the player searches the local network for NAS devices and shares. Ongoing action.
NETWORKFS.DELETE_DRIVE: Tooltip on the trash button in the network drives list, and title of the confirmation dialog that removes that NAS share from the player (files on the NAS are not deleted). Verb phrase.
NETWORKFS.EDIT_DRIVE: Tooltip on the pencil button in the network drives list (settings and wizard); opens the form to change that NAS share's settings. Verb phrase.
NETWORKFS.DELETE_DRIVE_CONFIRM: Fragment: start of the confirmation question in the Delete Drive dialog; code appends a space, the drive name, then '?'. Word order must allow the name at the end.
NETWORKFS.PLACEHOLDER_NAME: Placeholder text inside the name (alias) input of the add/edit network drive form; the display name for the NAS share. Noun.
NETWORKFS.PLACEHOLDER_IP_ADDRESS: Placeholder inside the host input of the add/edit network drive form: IP address or network hostname of the NAS. NAS = network storage device.
NETWORKFS.PLACEHOLDER_PATH_TO_SHARE: Placeholder inside the path input of the add/edit network drive form, showing the format of a share path on the NAS (folders separated by slashes). Keep the slashes.
NETWORKFS.ERROR_PATH_UNDEFINED: Warning toast (title: My Music) when saving a network drive without the share name or path filled in. Asks the user to enter it.
NETWORKFS.ERROR_UMOUNT: Error toast message (title: Error) when the player fails to disconnect and remove a network drive (NAS share). Share = network shared folder, noun.
NETWORKFS.MOUNT_SHARE_ERROR: Warning toast title when adding a network drive fails; the message below is the technical reason from the system.
NETWORKFS.NETWORK_DRIVE: Toast title for success messages about a network drive (NAS share), e.g. drive added or removed. Noun, singular.
NETWORKFS.REMOVED: Success toast message (title: Network Drive) after a NAS share is disconnected and removed from the player. Share = network shared folder, noun.
NETWORKFS.SHARE_MOUNT_SUCCESS: Success toast message (title: Network Drive) after a NAS share is added and connected; the library scan starts next.
NETWORKFS.SHARE_NOT_CONFIGURED: Error toast message (title: Error) when trying to remove a network drive that is not in the player's configuration. Share = network shared folder, noun.
NETWORK.NETWORK_STATUS: Panel title on the Network settings page of the classic web UI showing the current connections (Wi-Fi name, IP address, speed, online).
NETWORK.SSID: Label for the Wi-Fi network name (SSID, the technical term for it). Usually kept as the acronym. No render site found.
NETWORK.SIGNAL: Label for Wi-Fi signal strength of a network. Noun. No render site found.
NETWORK.IP_ADDRESS: Label in the Network Status panel, followed by ':' and the player's IP address on that connection.
NETWORK.SPEED: Label in the Network Status panel, followed by ':' and the connection speed (e.g. 1000 Mb/s).
NETWORK.ONLINE: Label in the Network Status panel, followed by ':' and a check or cross icon: whether the player can reach the internet. Adjective.
NETWORK.CONNECT: Button on a Wi-Fi network row (Network settings, first-run wizard) that joins that network; also a feature heading on the MyVolumio welcome page. Verb.
NETWORK.REFRESH: Button (and icon tooltip) under the Wi-Fi network list on the Network settings page; scans again for available networks. Verb.
NETWORK.OPEN_NETWORK: Tooltip on the unlocked padlock icon next to a Wi-Fi network: the network has no password. Open = unprotected, not 'open' as a verb.
NETWORK.SECURE_NETWORK: Tooltip on the locked padlock icon next to a Wi-Fi network: the network is password protected. Adjective + noun.
NETWORK.SECURITY: Label before the dropdown choosing a Wi-Fi security type (e.g. WPA2, open) when joining a hidden network by hand, in Network settings and the wizard. Noun.
NETWORK.MANUAL_WIFI_CONNECTION: Last row of the Wi-Fi network list (Network settings, wizard): tap to join a hidden network by typing its name, security type and password.
NETWORK.NETWORK_NAME: Placeholder in the input where the user types the name of a hidden Wi-Fi network to join manually. Noun.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_CONNECTION: Panel title on the Network settings page of the classic web UI above the list of Wi-Fi networks and the current connection.
NETWORK.AUTOMATIC_IP: Setting label (on/off switch) on the Network settings page, for wired and Wi-Fi: get the IP address automatically from the router (DHCP); off = enter a static IP.
NETWORK.AUTOMATIC_IP_DOC: Help text under the Automatic IP switch on the Network settings page. DHCP = router assigns the address; Static IP = fixed address typed by the user.
NETWORK.DNS_ERROR_INFO: Error toast message (title 'DNS Settings') on the Network settings page when custom DNS is on but the primary or secondary DNS server IP address is missing or too short.
NETWORK.DNS_SETTINGS: Section title on the Network settings page grouping the custom DNS server options; also the title of the toasts shown when saving them. DNS = server that turns domain names into IP addresses.
NETWORK.ENABLE_CUSTOM_DNS: Switch label in the DNS Settings section of the Network settings page; turns on use of user-chosen DNS servers instead of the ones provided by the router.
NETWORK.ENABLE_CUSTOM_DNS_DOC: Help text under the custom DNS switch on the Network settings page; webradios = internet radio stations, updates = system updates.
NETWORK.ENABLE_HOTSPOT: Switch label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page. Hotspot = Wi-Fi network the device creates itself so phones can connect to it directly for setup.
NETWORK.ENABLE_HOTSPOT_DOC: Help text under the Enable Hotspot switch on the Network settings page; 'dropped' = the Wi-Fi connection is lost.
NETWORK.GATEWAY: Input label for the router/gateway IP address in the static IP fields of the Wired and Wireless Network sections (shown when DHCP/automatic IP is off). Networking term.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_CHANNEL: Select label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page: the Wi-Fi radio channel (numbered frequency band) the device's own hotspot transmits on.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_CHANNEL_DOC: Help text under the Hotspot Channel select on the Network page; 'network-dense' = places with many nearby Wi-Fi networks causing interference.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_CONF_ERROR: Error toast title when saving Hotspot Settings fails validation (e.g. password too short).
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_FALLBACK: Switch label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page: start the hotspot as a fallback/backup whenever the Wi-Fi connection is lost. Noun phrase.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_FALLBACK_DOC: Help text under the Hotspot fallback switch on the Network settings page; 'unit' = the Volumio device.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_NAME: Input label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page: the network name (SSID) of the Wi-Fi hotspot the device creates.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_PASSWORD: Password input label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page: the key users type to join the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_PASSWORD_DOC: Help text under the Hotspot Password field on the Network settings page; passphrase = the hotspot's Wi-Fi password.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_PROTECTION: Switch label in Hotspot Settings on the Network page; when on, joining the device's hotspot requires a password.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_PW_LENGTH: Error toast message (title 'Hotspot Configuration Error') when the hotspot password entered on the Network settings page is shorter than 8 characters.
NETWORK.HOTSPOT_SETTINGS: Section title on the Network settings page grouping the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot options (enable, name, password, channel).
NETWORK.NETMASK: Input label for the subnet mask (e.g. 255.255.255.0) in the static IP fields of the Wired and Wireless Network sections. Networking term.
NETWORK.NETWORK_RESTART_ERROR: Error toast text when restarting the network connection fails; code appends the technical error message right after it, so keep the trailing colon and space.
NETWORK.NETWORK_RESTART_SUCCESS: Success toast message (title 'Network restart') after network settings are saved and the network connection is restarted.
NETWORK.NETWORK_RESTART_TITLE: Title of the success/error toasts shown when the device restarts its network connection after a settings change. Noun phrase.
NETWORK.NETWORK_SETTINGS: Page title of the Network settings page (wired, Wi-Fi, hotspot, DNS).
NETWORK.PRIMARY_DNS: Input label in DNS Settings on the Network page: IP address of the first (main) custom DNS server.
NETWORK.SECONDARYY_DNS: Input label in DNS Settings on the Network page: IP address of the second (backup) custom DNS server, used if the primary fails.
NETWORK.STATIC_IP: Label of the static IP address field in the Wired and Wireless Network sections, and title of the warning dialog shown when saving static IP settings. Fixed, manually set address.
NETWORK.STATIC_IP_WARNING: Body of the dialog (title 'Static IP') shown when saving manual IP settings on the Network page; 'unreachable' = the device can no longer be found on the network.
NETWORK.WIRED_NETWORK: Section title on the Network settings page for the Ethernet (cable) connection options: automatic IP (DHCP) or static IP.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_ENABLED: Switch label in the Wireless Network section of the Network page; turns the Wi-Fi radio on or off entirely.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_ENABLED_DOC: Help text under the Wireless Networking switch on the Network settings page; turning Wi-Fi off may reduce electrical noise and improve sound.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK: Section title on the Network settings page for the Wi-Fi connection options (enable Wi-Fi, automatic or static IP).
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_CONNECTION_DEFE: First-run wizard Wi-Fi step: start of a status sentence; code appends a space, the Wi-Fi network name, a space, then 'when first setup will be completed.'
First-run wizard Wi-Fi step: end of a status sentence, appended after a space and the Wi-Fi network name; the device joins that Wi-Fi only after setup finishes.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_CONNECTION_ERRO: Wi-Fi connection failure status (wizard and Network page); in the wizard code appends a space, the Wi-Fi network name, ', ' then 'Please retry or proceed to next step'.
First-run wizard Wi-Fi step: second half of a failure status, appended after 'Failed to connect to network <name>, '; user can try again or skip ahead.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_CONNECTION_SUCC: Wi-Fi connected status (wizard and Network page); in the wizard code appends a space, the Wi-Fi network name, ', ' then 'Please proceed to next step'.
First-run wizard Wi-Fi step: second half of the success status, appended after 'Successfully connected to network <name>, '; tells the user to go on.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_RESTART_ERROR: Error toast text when restarting the Wi-Fi service fails; code appends the technical error message right after it, so keep the trailing colon and space.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_RESTART_SUCCESS: Success toast message (title 'Wireless restart') after Wi-Fi settings are saved and the Wi-Fi connection is restarted.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_RESTART_TITLE: Title of the success/error toasts shown when the device restarts its Wi-Fi connection after a settings change. Noun phrase.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_CONNECTING_TO: Status message while the device joins a Wi-Fi network (setup wizard and Network settings). Code appends a space, the network name (SSID) and '... ', then a follow-up sentence like 'Please wait'.
NETWORK.WIRELESS_NETWORK_RESTART_AFTER_C: Second half of a setup-wizard message: follows 'Connecting to wireless network <name>... '. Warns the browser will lose the device; user must rejoin their home Wi-Fi and find the device again once it is connected.
WIZARD.LANGUAGE: Name of a first-run setup wizard step (navigation/step list) where the user picks the interface language. Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.NAME: Name of a first-run setup wizard step where the user names the device (the player's name on the network). Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.OUTPUT: Name of a first-run setup wizard step where the user picks the audio output (DAC, headphone jack, HDMI, USB). Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.NETWORK: Name of a first-run setup wizard step where the user connects the device to Wi-Fi. Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.MUSIC: Name of a first-run setup wizard step where the user adds music sources (USB drive or network drive). Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.FOLLOW: Name of a first-run setup wizard step inviting the user to follow Volumio on social media and join the mailing list. Imperative 'follow us' sense. No render site found.
WIZARD.DONE: Name of the last first-run setup wizard step (setup finished), or the button that closes the wizard. Short. No render site found.
WIZARD.WELCOME: Heading on the first screen of the first-run setup wizard (language step), above 'Select your language'; also the title of the first onboarding tour popover in the classic web UI.
WIZARD.SELECT_YOUR_LANGUAGE: Heading of the language step in the first-run setup wizard, above the dropdown of interface languages.
WIZARD.DEVICE_NAME: Heading of the name step in the first-run setup wizard, above a text field: the user gives the player a name that is unique on their home network.
WIZARD.DEVICE_ADDRESS: Line in the name step of the setup wizard, followed on the next line by the web address built from the chosen name (http://<name>.local). Keep the trailing colon.
WIZARD.SELECT_YOUR_AUDIO_OUTPUT: Heading of the output step in the first-run setup wizard, above a dropdown of audio outputs (e.g. headphone jack, HDMI, USB DAC).
WIZARD.SELECT_YOUR_I2S_DAC: Heading in the output step of the setup wizard, shown when the I2S DAC switch is on, above a dropdown of I2S DAC boards (add-on sound cards). I2S and DAC are technical names.
WIZARD.I_HAVE_DAC: Label above an on/off switch in the output step of the setup wizard: turn it on if an I2S DAC board (add-on sound card) is attached; it then shows the I2S DAC list.
WIZARD.CUSTOM_AMOUNT: Option on the final setup wizard step's donation form to enter one's own donation amount instead of a preset one. No render site found.
WIZARD.DONE_MESSAGE: Message on the last step of the first-run setup wizard saying setup is complete and the system is ready. 'syste' is a source typo for 'system'. No render site found.
WIZARD.MAIL_LIST_SUBSCRIPTION: Section heading in the Follow step of the setup wizard, above an email field and button to subscribe to Volumio's newsletter (mailing list).
WIZARD.SOCIAL_SHARE: Section heading in the Follow step of the setup wizard, above Twitter/Facebook buttons to share Volumio on social networks. 'Share' is the verb sense (post about it).
WIZARD.DONATE: Button on the last setup wizard step that opens a PayPal donation to support Volumio; also the start of a donation dialog title, followed by a space and the recipient's name.
WIZARD.SUBSCRIBED_SUCCESFULLY: Confirmation text in the Follow step of the setup wizard, shown after the user subscribed their email to Volumio's newsletter.
WIZARD.ADD_YOUR_MUSIC: Intro text of the Music step of the setup wizard, above the network drive panel: plug in a USB drive, or use the button below to add a network drive (NAS shared folder).
WIZARD.STEP: Word before the step counter in the setup wizard's bottom bar; code appends a space and the current position (e.g. '3/8'). Hidden on phones.
WIZARD.VOLUMIOAPPS: Name of a setup wizard step promoting the Volumio mobile apps (Android, iOS). Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.GET_APPS: Intro text of the Apps step in the setup wizard, above Google Play and App Store badges for the Volumio mobile apps.
WIZARD.WIFI_CONNECTION: Intro text of the Network step in the setup wizard, above the list of nearby Wi-Fi networks: pick the one the device should join.
WIZARD.DEVICECODE: Name of a setup wizard step where the user enters a device activation code shipped with the device. Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.DEVICE_CODE_TITLE: Heading of the activation code step in the setup wizard, above a field to enter the code that came with the device and unlocks extra features.
WIZARD.DEVICE_CODE_MESSAGE: Text in the activation code step of the setup wizard: if an activation code came with the device, enter it to unlock features reserved for its owner.
WIZARD.DEVICE_CODE_MESSAGE_CLICK: Sentence start in the activation code step of the setup wizard; code appends a space and the button name 'Validate Device Code'. Means: after typing the code, press that button.
WIZARD.DEVICE_CODE_VALIDATE: Button in the activation code step of the setup wizard that checks and applies the entered code; also quoted by name at the end of the 'Once done, click' sentence.
WIZARD.ERROR_ACTIVATING_DEVICE: Error text in the activation code step of the setup wizard; code appends ' : ' and the error returned by the server.
WIZARD.DEVICE_ACTIVATED: Success text in the activation code step of the setup wizard, shown after the code is accepted; the extra features are now unlocked.
WIZARD.ADVANCEDSETTINGS: Name of the setup wizard step where the user picks simple or full (advanced) settings mode. 'Experience' = user experience. Short noun. No render site found.
WIZARD.EXPERIENCE_SETTINGS_TITLE: Heading of the Experience step in the setup wizard, where the user chooses between a simplified or full (advanced) set of settings.
WIZARD.EXPERIENCE_SETTINGS_TEXT: Question in the Experience step of the setup wizard, above a dropdown: simplified settings (fewer options) or full control with all advanced settings.
WIZARD.EXPERIENCE_SETTINGS_TEXT_2: Small note under the question in the Experience step of the setup wizard: the simple/advanced choice can be changed later in System settings.
WIZARD.NO_NEED_DEVICE_CODE_MESSAGE: Note in the activation code step of the setup wizard: users who already entered their activation code before can skip this step.
WIZARD.LOGIN: Name of a setup wizard step, or button, to sign in to a MyVolumio account. Noun/verb ambiguity: here it means signing in. No render site found.
WIZARD.STREAMINGSERVICES: First-run wizard step title for the step where the user sets up where music comes from (streaming services, local and network storage). No render site found.
WIZARD.SELECT_YOUR_TIMEZONE: First-run wizard instruction/title asking the user to pick their time zone from a list. No render site found.
WIZARD.SOFTWAREUPDATE: First-run wizard step title about updating the device's system software (noun). No render site found.
WIZARD.AUTOMATIC_SOFTWAREUPDATE: Toggle label in the first-run wizard's software update step: install new system versions automatically. Noun phrase. No render site found.
WIZARD.AUTOMATIC_SOFTWAREUPDATE_DESC: Help text under the Automatic updates toggle in the wizard: when on, the device installs new system software by itself as soon as it is released. No render site found.
WIZARD.UPDATE_AVAILABLE: Status message in the first-run wizard's software update step: a newer system software version can be installed. No render site found.
WIZARD.CONGRATULATIONS: Heading on the last screen of the first-run setup wizard, celebrating that setup is complete.
